summary: Moves rich-text sanitising and allowed image types into new validation.php/config/validation.php (SVG and gif now allowed), adds validation to admin edit-user and site uploads, but deletes the end of app/Functions/functions.php (footer() unclosed -> parse error) and removes still-used block helper functions.

statements.text: ✖ block_text_translation_check() was deleted from app/Functions/functions.php, but resources/views/studio/edit-link.blade.php still uses it, so those pages will crash.
statements.why: Deleted in the diff; still called at edit-link.blade.php:81 at the commit and defined nowhere else.

statements.text: ✖ app/Functions/functions.php looks cut off: some of its { brackets are never closed, so it no longer runs. Every page that loads it will crash. Ask the agent to restore the end of the file.
statements.why: File ends inside footer() with no return/closing brace; autoloaded via composer files, footer() used in routes/web.php:77.

statements.text: ⚠ Uploads now accept SVG files (validation.php, config/validation.php). An SVG can carry a script that runs when opened from your site, so one user could attack others, admins included. Leave SVG out, or serve uploaded files from a separate domain.
statements.why: SVG added to allowed types for avatars/backgrounds/import; stored XSS risk.

statements.text: • The agent changed the admin edit user, admin site, studio page, studio background and import data parts of your server in ways plain can't describe yet.

misses.what: Other deleted block helpers (setBlockAssetContext, block_asset, block_text, bt) are also still used, so link blocks crash even if the syntax error is fixed; card names only block_text_translation_check.
Admin 'Edit user' now rejects saves when the password box is left empty (or no handle/email), because empty fields become null and fail the new 'string' rules.
Needs `composer dump-autoload` on deploy so validation.php is loaded.
Profile/page descriptions and text blocks go through a stricter HTML sanitizer; may strip formatting.
